title: Phase 6 · Error Detection & Correction
outline:
Phase 6 video (Algorithms, ECM3428): 'Error Detection & Correction', sub line 'How data survives a noisy wire'. 11 scenes, about 124 s: title (4), noise flips bits (10.5), parity (12.5), CRC: check bits from a long division (12.5), the receiver repeats the division (11), ask again or fix it yourself (11.5), valid words must stay far apart (14), Hamming: three checks, each guards a group (12.5), Hamming: the failed checks spell the position (14), Hamming fixes one error, not two (12.2), recap (9). Story: noise flips bits on a wire and the receiver cannot tell (scene 2); the cure is redundancy, extra check bits that depend on the data. A PARITY bit (the number of 1s made even) catches one flip but is fooled by two and never says where (3). A CRC divides the message by a pattern both sides know and sends the remainder (4); the receiver divides the whole frame again and a clean frame leaves 000, while two flips or a burst of three change the remainder (5). A failed check can mean 'ask again' (a download) but a far-away probe cannot wait for the reply, so its code must repair errors itself (6). Repair is possible when valid words are far apart: on the 3-bit cube only 000 and 111 are valid, three flips apart, so one flip leaves a word nearest its true word (repaired) but two flips lead to the wrong word (7). Hamming(7,4) puts check bits at positions 1, 2, 4, each a parity bit for the group of positions whose binary number has a 1 in its digit (8); after a flip the failed checks, read as binary p4 p2 p1, spell the position of the flipped bit and it is flipped back (9); with two flips the same rule points at an innocent third position and 'repairs' it wrongly: Hamming fixes exactly one error (10). Not covered (lessons 6.4, 6.6, 6.8, 6.9 and the workshop): generator polynomials, the guessing game, the G H M matrices, SECDED, Reed-Solomon / turbo / LDPC codes; the recap points to Workshop 6.W.

LESSONS the facts come from: a6-noise 6.1, a6-parity 6.2, a6-crc 6.3, a6-crcpoly 6.4, a6-distance 6.5, a6-game 6.6, a6-hamming 6.7, a6-matrix 6.8, a6-codes 6.9, a6-wire 6.W; js/content/algo/algo-p6.js, algo-p6-x-01..04.js, algo-workshops-6-03.js; bank js/bank/algo-*.js.

THE EXAMPLE DATA (all asserted when the page loads by videos/a6/common.js; a wrong number throws an Error). Bits are strings, tile index = position - 1.
 Scene 2: message 1011001 on the wire, the second bit (index 1) flips 0 -> 1: received 1111001.
 Scene 3 (lesson 6.3 strip): data 1011001 has four 1s so the even-parity bit is 0: frame 10110010. One flip (index 1): 11110010 has five 1s (odd: caught). Two flips (indices 1 and 4): 11111010 has six 1s (even: missed).
 Scenes 4-5 (lesson 6.3): message 1011, generator 1101 (degree 3: three check bits). Dividend 1011000: step 1 XOR 1101 under column 0 gives 0110000, step 2 XOR 1101 under column 1 gives 0000100: remainder 100; frame sent 1011100. The receiver divides 1011100: 0110100 then 0000000: remainder 000 (clean). Received 1111000 (flips 1 and 4, the pair that fooled parity): remainder 111. Received 1000000 (a burst of three, flips 2, 3, 4, the workshop's mission): remainder 110. Exhaustive audit of all 7-bit error patterns: 7 of 7 single flips, 21 of 21 double flips and 23 of 23 bursts of up to 3 bits change the remainder; a degree-16 generator catches every burst of 16 bits or fewer (lesson 6.4, CRC-16).
 Scene 6 (lesson 6.1 ARQ run): frame 11010010 (data 1101001 + parity 0); the fourth bit flips (11000010: three 1s, odd) so the receiver sends a NAK (here: 'send again') and the sender retransmits. A probe light-minutes away cannot wait: its code (the Hamming codeword 0110011) must repair itself.
 Scene 7 (lesson 6.5): the 3-bit cube, valid words 000 (bit 0) and 111 (bit 1), Hamming distance 3 (three flips apart: 000 -> 010 -> 011 -> 111). One flip 000 -> 010: distance to 000 is 1, to 111 is 2, so it decodes to 000 (right). Two flips 000 -> 011: distance to 000 is 2, to 111 is 1, so it decodes to 111 (wrong).
 Scenes 8-10 (lessons 6.7, 6.W): Hamming(7,4), positions 1-7, check bits p1 p2 p4 at positions 1, 2, 4, data 1011 at positions 3, 5, 6, 7, codeword 0110011. Groups: p1 = 1,3,5,7; p2 = 2,3,6,7; p4 = 4,5,6,7 (positions whose binary number ends in 1 / has a middle 1 / starts with 1; positions in binary 001 010 011 100 101 110 111). Each check bit makes its group's count of 1s even: p1 = 0 (data 1,0,1), p2 = 1 (data 1,1,1), p4 = 0 (data 0,1,1). One flip, position 6: 0110001; p4 group 0,0,0,1 (one 1) FAILS, p2 group 1,1,0,1 (three) FAILS, p1 group 0,1,0,1 (two) passes: p4 p2 p1 = 110 = 6, flip it back: 0110011. Two flips, positions 2 and 5: 0010111; every group holds three 1s so all three fail: 111 = 7, the 'repair' flips position 7 giving 0010110, which is itself a valid codeword (all three checks pass) with data 1110 instead of 1011 and three positions (2, 5, 7) wrong. Over all 16 codewords: all 112 single flips are repaired, none of the 336 double flips is (lesson 6.7 'Try every error').

VIDEO-WIDE CONVENTIONS. COLOURS (whole video): green = good (a clean word, a passed check, remainder 000, a repaired bit, a tick); red = bad (a flipped bit, a failed check, a wrong word, an alarm); blue = what is being counted or looked at; orange = a check bit / redundancy / attention (the parity bit, the CRC remainder, p1 p2 p4, a pointer); purple = the rule applied (the generator 1101, XOR, the group a check is reading); grey = neutral (data bits, things not in play). Every digit and label is 28 px or more; symbols (tick, cross, arrow, bolt, XOR sign, question mark) are SVG pictograms (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, A6.bolt / A6.xorIcon / A6.qmark), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure). The bit tiles are the video's vocabulary: a data bit is a grey tile, a check bit (parity bit, CRC remainder, p1 p2 p4) is an orange tile, a flipped bit is a red tile (tiles flip edge-on, switch digit and colour at the half-way point: A6.bits row.flip), a tile being counted is blue, the generator is purple. Position / tile indices are 0-based in code; Hamming positions in captions and labels are 1-based (position 6 = tile index 5). Scenes 8-10 share ONE layout (A6.hamRig) and the same codeword so the viewer follows one word from building it, to locating a flip, to the two-flip failure. The same two flips (the second and the fifth bit) fool parity in scene 3, are caught by the CRC in scene 5 and defeat Hamming in scene 10. Captions: one plain sentence each (at most 8 words, about 4 words per second at the fastest), and each caption starts only when the picture it describes is on screen. Words defined on screen before they are used: 'parity bit' (tag, scene 3), 'XOR' (tag 'XOR: differ = 1', scene 4), 'generator' and 'message' and 'remainder' (tags, scene 4), 'burst' (tag '3 in a row', scene 5), 'valid words' / '3 steps apart' (scene 7). The word 'syndrome' is never used: the failed checks 'spell the position'. scene-01-title.js is finished (a copy of the title card with a two-line 92 px headline because 'Error Detection & Correction' does not fit one line): do not replace it by VID.titleCard.

title: Noise flips bits,
and nobody tells you
caps: A message travels as bits.
Noise on the wire flips a bit.
The receiver cannot tell.
Fix: add a check bit.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: bits travelling along a wire can be flipped by noise, and the receiver sees only what arrives, so it cannot tell that anything changed. The cure (the rest of the video) is to send extra check bits that depend on the data. COLOURS (whole video): green = good (a clean word, a passed check, remainder 000, a repaired bit, a tick); red = bad (a flipped bit, a failed check, a wrong word, an alarm); blue = what is being counted or looked at; orange = a check bit / redundancy / attention (the parity bit, the CRC remainder, p1 p2 p4, a pointer); purple = the rule applied (the generator 1101, XOR, the group a check is reading); grey = neutral (data bits, things not in play). Every digit and label is 28 px or more; symbols (tick, cross, arrow, bolt, XOR sign, question mark) are SVG pictograms (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, A6.bolt / A6.xorIcon / A6.qmark), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure).

LAYOUT (stage px; sent word above, received word below, seven lanes between; a tag is about 58 px high). const sent = A6.bits(stage, {x: 150, y: 72, bits: A6.PARITY.frame, size: 84, gap: 12, tones: ['grey','grey','grey','grey','grey','grey','grey','orange']}): tile i at x = 150 + 96 i, y 72-156; tiles 0-6 are the message 1011001 (A6.WIRE.msg), tile 7 (x 822-906) is the orange check-bit slot: until 8.7 draw it as sent.set(7, {ghost: true, text: ''}) (dashed outline, empty). Tag A6.tag(stage, {x: 150, y: 0, text: 'sent', tone: 'grey'}) above the row. const received = A6.bits(stage, {x: 150, y: 388, bits: A6.WIRE.recv, size: 84, gap: 12}) (7 tiles, y 388-472, same x as the sent tiles above them) and A6.tag(stage, {x: 150, y: 486, text: 'received', tone: 'grey'}) under it. Lanes: const svg = L5.svg(stage); for i = 0..6 a grey arrow g_i = svg.appendChild(L5.arrow(192 + 96 i, 168, 192 + 96 i, 376, 'grey', 1, {w: 6, head: 18})) from the middle of sent tile i down to received tile i; L5.drawOn(g_i, k) draws it from the top. Noise: bolt = svg.appendChild(A6.bolt(288, 272, 130, 'orange')) on lane 1 (V.place(bolt, {s, o}) pops and fades it). Receiver's doubt: qmark = svg.appendChild(A6.qmark(470, 556, 96, 'orange')) and an orange tag A6.tag(stage, {x: 530, y: 536, text: 'any flips?', tone: 'orange'}). Final tag: A6.tag(stage, {x: 724, y: 166, text: 'check bit', tone: 'orange', solid: true}) under tile 7 (the lanes are gone by then).

TIMELINE. 0.2-0.5 the 'sent' tag pops; 0.3-0.9 sent tiles 0-6 pop in one after another (0.08 s apart, E.pop, grey); 0.8-1.1 the ghost slot fades in. 1.3-2.4 the seven lanes draw on (0.07 s apart, L5.drawOn, grey). 2.4-3.5 the bolt pops on lane 1 (s 0.5 -> 1.1 with E.pop over 0.5 s) and fades out 3.2-3.5; lane 1 shakes sideways +-4 px while it is hit (2.5-3.1). 3.0-3.6 the 'received' tag and the received tiles pop in (0.07 s apart); received tile 1 pops showing '0' (grey) and flips at 3.5-3.9 to '1' in RED with a small hop (received.flip(1, k, {from: '0', to: '1', tone: 'grey', toTone: 'red', hop: 14})); the other six stay grey. 5.4-5.9 the sent row, the 'sent' tag and the lanes fade out (o 1 -> 0): the receiver sees none of that; at 5.6 received tile 1 turns grey (no red: from here the received row looks like any word). 5.9-6.4 the orange qmark and the 'any flips?' tag pop in under the received row. 7.6-8.0 the received row, its tag, the qmark and the tag fade out. 8.0-8.5 the sent row and its tag fade back in (all eight slots, tile 7 still the ghost slot, no lanes). 8.7-9.4 the ghost slot becomes the orange check bit: sent.set(7, {text: '0', tone: 'orange', solid: true, s: E.pop(k)}); 9.1 the orange 'check bit' tag pops (k ramp). 9.4-10.5 hold.

title: One check bit
catches one flip
caps: Count the 1s in the message.
Add a bit that makes the total even.
One flip makes the total odd: caught.
But which bit? Parity cannot say.
Two flips cancel out: missed.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: a parity bit makes the number of 1s even. One flip makes it odd, so the receiver sees an alarm, but it cannot say which bit; a second flip makes it even again and parity is fooled. COLOURS (whole video): green = good (a clean word, a passed check, remainder 000, a repaired bit, a tick); red = bad (a flipped bit, a failed check, a wrong word, an alarm); blue = what is being counted or looked at; orange = a check bit / redundancy / attention (the parity bit, the CRC remainder, p1 p2 p4, a pointer); purple = the rule applied (the generator 1101, XOR, the group a check is reading); grey = neutral (data bits, things not in play). Every digit and label is 28 px or more; symbols (tick, cross, arrow, bolt, XOR sign, question mark) are SVG pictograms (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, A6.bolt / A6.xorIcon / A6.qmark), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure).

LAYOUT (stage px; a tag is about 58 px high). const row = A6.bits(stage, {x: 42, y: 150, bits: A6.PARITY.frame, size: 96, gap: 12, tones: ['grey' x7, 'orange']}) (tile i at x = 42 + 108 i, y 150-246; tile 7 at x 798-894 is the parity bit, orange; tiles 0-6 the message 1011001). Tag A6.tag(stage, {x: 724, y: 264, text: 'parity bit', tone: 'orange', solid: true}) under tile 7. Counter const ones = A6.stat(stage, {x: 42, y: 400, w: 270, h: 80, label: 'ones', tone: 'blue'}); verdict const badge = L5.badge(stage, {x: 330, y: 406, w: 420, h: 68, valid: 'even: looks fine', invalid: 'odd: alarm'}) (badge('valid' | 'invalid' | 'none', k)); a red tag A6.tag(stage, {x: 770, y: 411, text: 'missed', tone: 'red', solid: true}). Question marks: eight A6.qmark(row.mid(i).x, 102, 60, 'orange') in an L5.svg layer, one above every tile (y 72-132).

DATA: frame A6.PARITY.frame = '10110010'; the 1s of the message are tiles 0, 2, 3, 6 (A6.PARITY.ones = 4, even, so the parity bit is 0). One flip: A6.PARITY.one = {flips: [1], recv: '11110010', ones: 5, caught: true}. Two flips: A6.PARITY.two = {flips: [1, 4], recv: '11111010', ones: 6, caught: false}. The counter always shows ones(current word) (A6.ones), including the parity bit.

TIMELINE. 0.2-0.9 tiles 0-6 pop (0.07 s apart, grey); tile 7 is the ghost slot (dashed orange, empty text) from 0.8. 1.0-1.4 the 'ones' counter pops reading 0. Counting: at 1.2, 1.6, 2.0, 2.4 the four 1s (tiles 0, 2, 3, 6) turn blue (tone 'blue', s bump 1.12 over 0.3 s via V.flash) and the counter reads 1, 2, 3, 4 (bump each time). 2.9-3.5 tile 7 becomes the orange solid parity bit '0' (E.pop) and the 'parity bit' tag pops at 3.3; 3.6-4.0 the counter turns green (tone 'green') and the badge pops 'valid' (green tick, 'even: looks fine'). ONE FLIP: 5.4-5.9 tile 1 flips '0' -> '1' to RED with a hop (row.flip(1, k, {from: '0', to: '1', tone: 'grey', toTone: 'red', hop: 14})); 5.9 the counter reads 5 and turns red (bump); 6.0-6.4 the badge switches to 'invalid' (red cross, 'odd: alarm'). WHICH BIT: 8.0-8.6 the eight orange question marks pop over the tiles (0.05 s apart); 9.7-10.0 they fade out. SECOND FLIP: 10.0-10.5 tile 4 flips '0' -> '1' red (hop 14) while tile 1 stays red; 10.5 the counter reads 6 and turns green; 10.6-11.0 the badge goes back to 'valid' (green, 'even: looks fine') even though two tiles are red; 11.1-11.5 the red 'missed' tag pops. 11.5-12.5 hold.

END STATE: two red tiles, a green 'even: looks fine' badge and the red 'missed' tag: parity was fooled. Parity cannot say.'],[10.7,12.4,'Two flips cancel out: missed.']]

title: Check bits come from
a long division
caps: Pick a pattern both sides know.
Add zeros to the message, then divide.
Line the pattern up under the next 1.
What is left over is the remainder.
Send the message plus the remainder.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: a CRC check is the remainder of a long division of the message by a pattern (the generator) both sides know, where 'subtract' is XOR (no borrowing). The sender appends zeros, divides, and sends the message followed by the remainder. Run for real on message 1011, generator 1101. COLOURS (whole video): green = good (a clean word, a passed check, remainder 000, a repaired bit, a tick); red = bad (a flipped bit, a failed check, a wrong word, an alarm); blue = what is being counted or looked at; orange = a check bit / redundancy / attention (the parity bit, the CRC remainder, p1 p2 p4, a pointer); purple = the rule applied (the generator 1101, XOR, the group a check is reading); grey = neutral (data bits, things not in play). Every digit and label is 28 px or more; symbols (tick, cross, arrow, bolt, XOR sign, question mark) are SVG pictograms (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, A6.bolt / A6.xorIcon / A6.qmark), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure).

LAYOUT (stage px; a tag is about 58 px high). THE DIVISION on the left: const d = A6.division(stage, {x: 80, y: 76, dividend: A6.CRC.padded, gen: A6.CRC.gen, size: 60, gap: 8, rowGap: 14, padFrom: 4}) (five rows at y 76, 150, 224, 298, 372, each 60 high; tile columns x 80, 148, ..., 488; XOR signs at x 50; d.update({p, padK, msgK, remK})). Tag A6.tag(stage, {x: 352, y: 10, text: 'add 000', tone: 'orange'}) above the three orange zero tiles. RIGHT COLUMN (x 600-924): A6.tag(stage, {x: 600, y: 8, text: 'message', tone: 'grey'}) and msg = A6.bits(stage, {x: 600, y: 76, bits: A6.CRC.msg, size: 60, gap: 8}); A6.tag(stage, {x: 600, y: 150, text: 'generator', tone: 'purple'}) and gen = A6.bits(stage, {x: 600, y: 218, bits: A6.CRC.gen, size: 60, gap: 8, tone: 'purple'}); A6.tag(stage, {x: 590, y: 300, text: 'XOR: differ = 1', tone: 'purple'}). Tag A6.tag(stage, {x: 562, y: 378, text: 'remainder', tone: 'orange', solid: true}) beside the last row. THE FRAME at the bottom: const out = A6.bits(stage, {x: 186, y: 520, bits: A6.CRC.frame, size: 72, gap: 10, tones: ['grey','grey','grey','grey','orange','orange','orange']}) (tile i at x = 186 + 82 i) with A6.tag(stage, {x: 186, y: 456, text: 'frame sent', tone: 'green'}) above it.

DATA (assert with A6.same): A6.CRC.padded = '1011000', gen '1101', steps: col 0 '1011000' xor '1101000' = '0110000'; col 1 '0110000' xor '0110100' = '0000100'; A6.CRC.rem = '100' (the last three tiles of the last row); A6.CRC.frame = '1011100'. d.update draws exactly these rows.

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.1 the 'message' tag and msg tiles pop (0.08 s apart); 0.7-1.6 the 'generator' tag and the purple gen tiles pop. 1.9-2.5 d.update({msgK}) pops the four message tiles of row 0 (msgK 0 -> 1); 2.5-3.0 padK 0 -> 1 pops the three orange zeros; the 'add 000' tag pops at 2.6. STEP 1: p = (t - 3.2) / 2.2 over 3.2-5.4 (3.2-4.3 the first four bits of row 0 are ringed purple and the generator row slides in under them with its XOR sign; 4.3-5.4 the result row flips in); the 'XOR: differ = 1' tag pops at 3.6. STEP 2: p = 1 + (t - 5.5) / 2.2 over 5.5-7.7 (the generator now sits one column further right, under the next 1). 7.9-8.6 d.update({remK: 0 -> 1}) turns the last three tiles of the last row solid orange with a bounce; the 'remainder' tag pops at 8.1. 8.9-9.8 the frame row: tiles 0-3 fly from the message tiles at the right (msg.mid(i)) and tiles 4-6 from the remainder tiles (d.mid(d.last, i)) to their slots (offset = start - end shrinking to 0 with E.inOut, scale 0.83 -> 1, o 0 -> 1 over the first 0.2 s); the 'frame sent' tag pops at 9.6. 10.0-12.5 hold (everything stays; calm).

END STATE: the division stack with the orange remainder 100, the frame 1011 + 100 below it. Scene 5 re-uses this frame. title: The receiver repeats
the division
caps: Divide the frame by the same pattern.
Even two flips change the remainder.
A burst of three is caught too.
More check bits catch longer bursts.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: the receiver divides what arrives by the same pattern. A clean frame leaves remainder 000; the two flips that fooled parity, and a burst of three bits in a row, both change the remainder. More check bits catch longer bursts. The long division itself was shown in scene 4: here only its result is shown (the remainder tiles flip to the computed values). COLOURS (whole video): green = good (a clean word, a passed check, remainder 000, a repaired bit, a tick); red = bad (a flipped bit, a failed check, a wrong word, an alarm); blue = what is being counted or looked at; orange = a check bit / redundancy / attention (the parity bit, the CRC remainder, p1 p2 p4, a pointer); purple = the rule applied (the generator 1101, XOR, the group a check is reading); grey = neutral (data bits, things not in play). Every digit and label is 28 px or more; symbols (tick, cross, arrow, bolt, XOR sign, question mark) are SVG pictograms (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, A6.bolt / A6.xorIcon / A6.qmark), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure).

Purple arrow const svg = L5.svg(stage); svg.appendChild(L5.arrow(468, 176, 468, 292, 'purple', 1, {w: 8, head: 24})) with the purple tag A6.tag(stage, {x: 496, y: 214, text: 'divide by 1101', tone: 'purple'}). const rem = A6.bits(stage, {x: 330, y: 304, bits: '000', size: 84, gap: 12}) (x 330-606, y 304-388) with the orange tag A6.tag(stage, {x: 100, y: 322, text: 'remainder', tone: 'orange'}). const badge = L5.badge(stage, {x: 640, y: 312, w: 280, h: 68, valid: 'clean', invalid: 'error found'}). DATA (assert with A6.same): A6.CRC.cases = clean {recv '1011100', rem '000'}, two {flips [1, 4], recv '1111000', rem '111'}, burst {flips [2, 3, 4], recv '1000000', rem '110'}; A6.CRC.audit = {singles: [7, 7], doubles: [21, 21], bursts: [23, 23]} (assert; the bottom tags state this rule: the burst length caught is the number of check bits; '16 check bits: every burst up to 16' is lesson 6.4's CRC-16). RESET: 5.4-5.9 tiles 1 and 4 flip back to their normal look, the remainder tiles flip back to green '000' and the badge shows 'valid' again. title: Ask again,
or fix it yourself
caps: A download checks every frame.
Check fails, so ask for a resend.
A probe far away cannot wait.
So it must repair errors itself.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: detection alone works when the receiver can ask for the frame again (a download); when it cannot wait for the answer (a probe light-minutes away) the code must repair errors by itself, which is what the rest of the video builds. Two stacked panels, played one after the other. caps: One flip is one step.

IDEA: a code can repair a flipped bit only if its valid words are far apart. title: Three checks,
each guards a group
caps: Check bits sit at positions 1, 2, 4.
Write each position in binary.
p4 guards positions starting with 1.
p2 guards positions with a middle 1.
p1 guards positions ending in 1.
Every group now has an even count.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: Hamming(7,4) sends 4 data bits with 3 check bits. The check bits sit at positions 1, 2 and 4; each guards the group of positions whose binary number has a 1 in its own digit (p4 the first digit, p2 the middle, p1 the last) and is set so the group's count of 1s is even. Building the codeword 0110011 from data 1011. COLOURS (whole video): green = good (a clean word, a passed check, remainder 000, a repaired bit, a tick); red = bad (a flipped bit, a failed check, a wrong word, an alarm); blue = what is being counted or looked at; orange = a check bit / redundancy / attention (the parity bit, the CRC remainder, p1 p2 p4, a pointer); purple = the rule applied (the generator 1101, XOR, the group a check is reading); grey = neutral (data bits, things not in play). Tile texts you draw every frame: check tiles (positions 1, 2, 4) show 'p1', 'p2', 'p4' until their value is computed, data tiles show A6.HAM.cw[i] (positions 3, 5, 6, 7 = 1, 0, 1, 1). Use H.all((i) => ({text, tone: i + 1 in [1,2,4] ? 'orange' : 'grey', ring, ringK, ...})) and H.bits.flip(i, k, {from: 'p4', to: '0', tone: 'orange', toTone: 'orange', hop: 10}) for the reveals. For each band H.row(name, {k, dots, vals, own, tone, verdict, vk}): vals = the 7-character current word (the discs show its digits at the watched positions) with own: '?' while the check bit is unknown, tone 'purple' while that band is being read and 'grey' afterwards.

(disc); the word used for vals before its reveal can hold 0 for the unknown check bits.

helpers:
FILES: videos/a6/common.js (pure data and algorithms, no DOM, every number asserted at load), common-2.js (tiles, labels, tags, counters, icons), common-3.js (the long-division widget), common-4.js (the Hamming rig, the syndrome readout, the cube). Everything hangs off window.VID.a6; scenes start with const V = window.VID, A6 = V.a6, L5 = V.l5 and const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. videos/algo-6.html loads engine.js, cards.js, l5/common.js, then a6/common.js ... common-4.js, then scene-01 ... scene-11, audio/algo-6.js. l6 is not loaded. Every helper file starts with a long API comment listing every signature, option and return value: READ THEM FIRST, they are the contract. All draw calls are pure: call them every frame from update(t) with everything you want to see; nothing is remembered between frames; no Math.random, Date or timers.

A. DATA (common.js): A6.bitsOf / str / ones / parityOf / flipAt(s, ...idx) / diffAt / dist / polyMod / divide(bits, gen) -> {rows, steps, rem}; A6.WIRE, A6.PARITY {data, p, frame, ones, one, two}, A6.CRC {msg, gen, padded, steps, rem, frame, cases [clean, two, burst], audit, div, recvDiv(case)}, A6.ARQ, A6.CUBE_NODES / CUBE_EDGES / CODE {words, d, path, one, two} / dist / nearest / RATE, A6.HAM {data, cw, checkPos, dataPos, groups, bin, encode, one, two, every} with A6.hEnc / hCheck / hChecks / hSyn / hFix / hData; A6.same / A6.close (build-time asserts that throw clear Errors), A6.rng, A6.pos(i) / A6.idx(p). Tile index = bit index (0-based); Hamming positions are 1-based.
